title: SPINAL MUSCULAR ATROPHY WITH CONGENITAL BONE FRACTURES 2

relationships.phenotype: SPINAL MUSCULAR ATROPHY WITH CONGENITAL BONE FRACTURES 2

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 (SMABF2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ASCC1 gene on chromosome 10q22.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 (SMABF2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ASCC1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract links ASCC1 mutations to the disease. It doesn't say whether the ASCC1 mutations were homozygous, and it doesn't use the SMABF2 label.

checks.claim: The ASCC1 gene is located on chromosome 10q22.
checks.evidence_quote: This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. It is accepted as standard nomenclature for ASCC1.

paragraphs.text: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is a severe autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder that begins before birth. It is characterized by fetal hypokinesia, generalized hypotonia and muscle weakness, arthrogryposis, and congenital fractures of the long bones. Affected infants have respiratory insufficiency and usually die early.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is a severe autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: A similar disorder was described in patients with recessive variants in two genes: TRIP4 (three families) and ASCC1 (one family)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a severe neuromuscular disorder caused by recessive variants (homozygous in the patient).

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 begins before birth.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)
checks.explanation: The abstract states the onset is prenatal.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is characterized by fetal hypokinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: lack of spontaneous movements
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a lack of spontaneous movements in the newborn but does not mention fetal hypokinesia.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is characterized by generalized hypotonia and muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient presented generalized hypotonia
checks.explanation: Generalized hypotonia is stated. Muscle weakness is not mentioned.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is characterized by arthrogryposis.
checks.evidence_quote: multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita)
checks.explanation: The abstract names arthrogryposis.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is characterized by congenital fractures of the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: prenatal fractures of the long bones
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Infants with spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 have respiratory insufficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures
checks.explanation: The abstract reports respiratory distress.

checks.claim: Infants with spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 usually die early.
checks.evidence_quote: She died within the first days of life.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports early death for this one patient. It does not describe early death as the usual course.

paragraphs.text: Knierim et al. (2016) reported patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures. Features included reduced fetal movements, severe hypotonia at birth, arthrogryposis, congenital fractures, and respiratory failure resulting in early death.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) reported patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures reported by Knierim et al. (2016) had reduced fetal movements.
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't mention reduced fetal movements.

checks.claim: The patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures reported by Knierim et al. (2016) had severe hypotonia at birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't mention hypotonia at birth.

checks.claim: The patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures reported by Knierim et al. (2016) had arthrogryposis.
checks.evidence_quote: multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita)
checks.explanation: The abstract names arthrogryposis.

checks.claim: The patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures reported by Knierim et al. (2016) had congenital fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures
checks.explanation: The abstract states congenital fractures.

checks.claim: The patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures reported by Knierim et al. (2016) had respiratory failure resulting in early death.
checks.evidence_quote: respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures
checks.explanation: Respiratory distress is reported, but the abstract doesn't say it led to early death.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of SMABF2 in the family reported by Knierim et al. (2016) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of SMABF2 in the family reported by Knierim et al. (2016) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1)
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is supported. The abstract describes four families, not one, and doesn't say which families carried ASCC1 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-1 (SMABF1) is caused by mutation in the TRIP4 gene, which encodes another subunit of the activating signal cointegrator-1 (ASC-1) complex.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-1 (SMABF1) is caused by mutation in the TRIP4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.
checks.explanation: TRIP4 mutations are associated with the disease. The abstract doesn't use the SMABF1 designation.

checks.claim: The TRIP4 gene encodes a subunit of the activating signal cointegrator-1 (ASC-1) complex, as does ASCC1.
checks.evidence_quote: two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Knierim et al. (2016) found homozygous loss-of-function mutations in genes encoding subunits of the ASC-1 complex in patients with prenatal spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures. The patients with SMABF2 carried mutations in the ASCC1 gene, and the patients with SMABF1 carried mutations in TRIP4. Knierim et al. (2016) linked the disorder to impaired function of the ASC-1 transcriptional coactivator complex.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) found homozygous loss-of-function mutations in genes encoding subunits of the ASC-1 complex in patients with prenatal spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins
checks.explanation: The abstract reports both homozygous and compound-heterozygous mutations, not only homozygous ones.

checks.claim: In the study by Knierim et al. (2016), the patients with SMABF2 carried mutations in the ASCC1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations
checks.explanation: ASCC1 mutations were found, but the abstract doesn't split patients into SMABF2 and SMABF1 groups.

checks.claim: In the study by Knierim et al. (2016), the patients with SMABF1 carried mutations in the TRIP4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations
checks.explanation: TRIP4 mutations were found, but the abstract doesn't split patients into SMABF2 and SMABF1 groups.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) linked prenatal spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures to impaired function of the ASC-1 transcriptional coactivator complex.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings indicate that the dysfunction of a transcriptional coactivator complex can result in a clinical syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion directly.
